messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy window start: service-x v2.3.1 -> canary 20% (NA+APAC). Feature flag `split_cache_mode` default=OFF. Rolling with pinned-routing to v2.3.1 for canary.
sam (eng): Runbook: canary ramp 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 8m soak. Safety hold at 20% requires SRE ack. Health gates: p99 latency, error rate, downstream timeout rate.
joel (pm): Note: this enables the split cache path for small cohorts only. Release notes: https://go/release-notes/service-x/v2.3.1 (short).
lina (sre): Preflight checks green. Setting alerts and trace sampling to 100% for canary cohorts.
priya (eng-releases): Added greylist for internal cohorts; will exclude corp-internal traffic. Pin set: routing->v2.3.1 for canary; fallback: v2.2.x.
sam (eng): Command: `/ff set split_cache_mode --percent 20 --regions na,apac --by deploybot`
deploy-bot: Executing: `/ff set split_cache_mode --percent 20 --regions na,apac --by deploybot`
deploy-bot: Result: OK — split_cache_mode = 20% (na,apac). Canary routing pinned to v2.3.1.
joel (pm): Quick telemetry note: synthetic p99 jumped from 160ms -> 420ms in APAC within 2m of flip. Not huge user impact on volume but visible.
lina (sre): Confirming real traffic p99 spike in APAC, error budget burn starting. I'm holding further ramp.
sam (eng): Looking at traces: cache shard lookup falling back to remote for certain key ranges causing tail latency. Might be a shard mapping bug.
priya (eng-releases): Given spike, recommend immediate rollback to 0% for APAC while NA stays at 20% for more time. Thoughts?
joel (pm): Prefer conservative approach: rollback APAC to 0% and leave NA at 10% while we hotfix. We want to avoid widespread rollback.
lina (sre): I can approve APAC rollback. Set NA to 10% to reduce blast radius.
sam (eng): Commands: `/ff set split_cache_mode --percent 0 --regions apac --by deploybot` and `/ff set split_cache_mode --percent 10 --regions na --by deploybot`
deploy-bot: Executing: `/ff set split_cache_mode --percent 0 --regions apac --by deploybot`
deploy-bot: Result: OK — split_cache_mode = 0% (apac). Canary drained in APAC.
deploy-bot: Executing: `/ff set split_cache_mode --percent 10 --regions na --by deploybot`
deploy-bot: Result: OK — split_cache_mode = 10% (na).
priya (eng-releases): Marked release v2.3.1 as partial-rollout: APAC rolled back due to cache shard fallback; NA reduced to 10%. Added incident tag: INC-2026-307.
joel (pm): I'll update customer-facing notes after watch window. Keep me in loop if NA p99 rises.
lina (sre): After APAC rollback p99 normalized. NA still slightly elevated but within threshold; continuing 30m watch.
sam (eng): Root cause hypothesis: missing shard mapping in the new router when keyspace > X. Preparing a patch to fallback mapping and will run a targeted unit test.
priya (eng-releases): Scheduling retry: next low-traffic window Sun 04:00-05:00 UTC. Plan: staged APAC -> NA with feature gated to cohort ids list. Will require explicit SRE ack at 20% and 50%.
joel (pm): Add me and support to the retry run. Also include a short blurb for support on how to force-unwind the flag: `/ff set split_cache_mode --percent 0 --regions all --by support-bot`
sam (eng): I'll create a canary-only pin: `/deploy pin service-x --version v2.3.1 --scope canary --until 2026-06-07T06:00Z`
deploy-bot: Pin created: service-x pinned to v2.3.1 (canary) until 2026-06-07T06:00Z.
lina (sre): TL;DR: partial rollback done, APAC drained, NA reduced. Watch window 30m. Retry scheduled with cohort gating and manual holds. I'll file a short post-incident note once watch completes.
joel (pm): Thanks team. Please capture commands used in the release notes and the exact timeline for the customer update.
priya (eng-releases): Done — release tracker updated with timeline, commands, incident id, and retry window. Closing this thread; reopen when retry starts. :white_check_mark:
